cases.prompt: A colleague's aseptic medium-change record reads: 'Cabinet UV 15 min; both cell lines handled to save time; lot B expired but clear so used; cap set face down on bench; one pipette used for turbid flask, target flask and fresh medium; culture looked slightly cloudy so penicillin-streptomycin added; waste poured to sink; mycoplasma test not submitted because medium was 0.22 µm filtered.' Write a review of this record: identify the pre-work, layout and manipulation failures; state what should have been done before, during and after the change; explain what clear medium and 0.22 µm filtration do and do not prove; and specify containment, waste, testing and cleanup actions.

rubric.criterion: Identifies the pre-work and layout failures: UV used instead of chemical wiping, two cell lines, expired medium and unwiped or improperly arranged items
Identifies the sterile-to-sterile failures: face-down closure, one pipette reused across turbid, target and fresh medium, and the missing side-approach/slow-motion/glove-sanitization controls
Explains that clear medium and a 0.22 µm filter label do not prove freedom from mollicutes, and that a dedicated mycoplasma test plus valid sterility incubation are the appropriate evidence
States the correct incubation schedule: at least 14 days within 20–35 °C, with at least 7 days at 20–25 °C followed by at least 7 days at 30–35 °C
Rejects antibiotic rescue and specifies containment, sealed decontaminated disposal, waste decontamination, cabinet cleanup and incident review

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic record; it is not a grade or a competency record, and your laboratory's procedures govern real contamination responses.

cases.prompt: A colleague's count record for a synthetic suspension reads: 20 µL cells + 30 µL trypan blue; chamber A 22 cells, chamber B 61 cells (one large square each); blue cells on the right edge counted as dead; 'viability 96%, culture healthy, seed tomorrow'. Write a review of this record: what you would check or redo before trusting the count, how you would calculate and report concentration, viability and counting uncertainty, and what the viability figure can and cannot support.

rubric.criterion: Uses the dilution factor (20 + 30)/20 = 2.5 and the chamber's stated volume per large square, and asks whether the suspension was mixed before sampling
Recognises that 22 and 61 differ by far more than √(22 + 61) ≈ 9.1, so the chambers should be reloaded rather than averaged
Corrects the boundary error: cells touching the right edge are excluded before any stain decision, so the stained tally and viability must be recounted
Reports viable concentration, viability and the Poisson uncertainty with the N it was computed from, and notes the systematic errors that uncertainty excludes
States that trypan-blue exclusion shows membrane integrity at counting time and cannot establish health, growth, phenotype or freedom from contamination

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic record; it is not a grade or a competency record, and your laboratory's procedures govern real counts.

cases.prompt: A synthetic preparation record states: “500 mL final complete medium: 500 mL basal + 50 mL serum + 5 mL glutamine; glutamine aliquot had been at room temperature overnight; pH acceptable because colour red, osmolality not measured; serum heat-inactivated to make it defined and sterile; 0.45 µm filter, visual inspection only; filtrate collected in an unlabelled bottle; 50 mL aliquots promised from 400 mL recovered; label says complete medium; stored at 22 °C in light and released immediately; no sterility or mycoplasma controls.” Write a corrected batch plan and evidence review. Recalculate every addition and the basal volume; distinguish formulation and physicochemical issues; evaluate supplement and heat-inactivation decisions; specify filtration, integrity, control and dedicated-test evidence; and repair aliquot, label, storage, expiry and release decisions. State which values would come from the actual product and cell-line procedure rather than from this synthetic scenario.

rubric.criterion: Explains basal nutrient roles, why red colour does not replace pH or osmolality measurement, the bicarbonate/CO₂ relationship, and why serum-free, heat-inactivated and chemically defined are different descriptions
Recomputes the intended final batch as 50 mL serum + 5 mL 100× glutamine + 445 mL basal = 500 mL, and identifies the record’s erroneous 555 mL total
Rejects the room-temperature glutamine history and universal heat-inactivation rationale; requires lot/storage/thaw traceability, limited freeze–thaw exposure and dedicated reagents for one cell line

Specifies an aseptic 0.22 µm protein-compatible filter with a supported integrity test, valid 14-day lower-then-higher-temperature sterility controls and dedicated mycoplasma testing, without treating clarity as proof

Rejects over-allocation and immediate release; requires complete formulation/date/expiry/batch/component-lot labelling, feasible aliquot accounting, light-protected 2–8 °C storage and quarantine pending acceptable QC

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic record; it is not a grade, a competency record or physical validation, and actual product instructions, cell-line requirements and institutional procedures govern real media preparation.

cases.prompt: A synthetic passage record states: “95% confluent; routine passage mandatory because viability will be high. Washed with complete medium; enzyme-based dissociation for 10 min; no neutralization before collection. Resuspended in 6.0 mL; 10 µL cells + 10 µL trypan blue; A 58 unstained + 5 stained, B 63 + 4. Two T-75 flasks, each target 5.00 × 10⁵ viable cells in 12.0 mL final volume. Add 0.826 mL cell suspension plus 12 mL fresh medium to each flask. Label both passage 12, unchanged PDL; no need to consider previous passage 12, cumulative PDL 18, or N0 = 1.815 × 10⁶. Repeated passage cannot affect identity.” Write a zero-point self-review: evaluate the disposition and harvest decisions; independently recompute concentration, viability, viable yield and per-flask inoculum/fresh medium; correct the passage and PDL record; and identify which claims still require separate evidence.

rubric.criterion: Rejects routine passaging under the declared 95% scenario and identifies the complete-medium wash, 10-minute exposure and absent neutralization as departures from the lesson workflow
Recomputes twofold dilution, mean unstained count (58 + 63)/2 = 60.5, viable concentration 1.21 × 10⁶ cells/mL, viability 121/130 × 100 = 93.1%, and viable yield 7.26 × 10⁶ in 6.0 mL
Calculates 0.413223 mL cell suspension and 11.586777 mL fresh medium per flask, explaining why 0.826 mL per flask is the two-flask amount and why adding 12 mL overshoots the final volume
Increments passage 12 to 13 and computes log₂(7.26/1.815) = 2, hence cumulative PDL 18 + 2 = 20, while distinguishing these from a split ratio

States that viability, PDL and simulation checkpoints do not establish identity, sterility, genomic stability, future growth or physical technique; repeated-subculture concerns require records and later authentication/quality review

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic record; it is not a grade or competency record, and cell-line instructions and institutional procedures govern real passaging.

cases.prompt: A synthetic freeze/thaw record states: “The harvest has 1.00 × 10⁷ viable cells at 95.0% viability. Make four vials; each contains 2.50 × 10⁶ viable cells per vial in 1.00 mL, separately from the batch concentration of 2.50 × 10⁶ cells/mL. For 4.00 mL final freeze medium at 10.0% v/v DMSO, combine 4.00 mL base with 0.400 mL DMSO at 22 °C in one rapid addition. Place uncovered vials in a −80 °C freezer, then immerse them in LN₂; location ‘nitrogen’. Thaw at 22 °C for 20 min, add 9.00 mL medium rapidly, leave all DMSO, and resuspend in 2.00 mL. The panel shows 92.0% viability. Claim 2.30 × 10⁶ viable cells recovered and 1.00% residual DMSO, then release the working stock because viability is high.” Write a zero-point self-review: correct each process decision; independently recompute DMSO/base volumes, aliquot concentration, diluted and residual DMSO under a stated removal assumption, and viable recovery/concentration; specify storage/location, recount, quarantine and bank-tier records; and state the evidence limits.

rubric.criterion: Identifies warm rapid DMSO addition, uncontrolled cooling, liquid-phase storage, slow thaw, abrupt dilution and absent DMSO removal as mistakes, explaining permeating-agent toxicity/osmotic handling and the two cooling-injury mechanisms

Recomputes 2.50 × 10⁶ viable cells per vial for each of four vials and, separately, 2.50 × 10⁶ cells/mL batch concentration; also computes 0.400 mL DMSO plus 3.60 mL base for a 4.00 mL final batch and 1.00% DMSO after 1.00 mL is added to 9.00 mL medium
Using the explicitly assumed 95.0% DMSO-solute removal, computes 0.00500 mL remaining and 0.250% v/v in 2.00 mL; rejects the record’s unsupported residual claim
Computes recovered viable cells 2.50 × 10⁶ × 92.0/95.0 = 2.421053 × 10⁶ and concentration 1.210526 × 10⁶ cells/mL in 2.00 mL, explaining why 2.30 × 10⁶ omits pre-freeze viability

Selects vapour storage with a complete synthetic address, treats the recount as membrane integrity only, retains quarantine pending sterility/QC and a working-stock/bank-tier forward record, and claims no physical technique or release competency

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic record; it is not a grade, competency record, physical validation or QC release decision. Cell-specific instructions and institutional procedures govern real work.

cases.prompt: A synthetic incident note says: “Five incoming flasks remained in the clean incubator because no organism had been named. Flask P is turbid and acidic; flask Q has branching filaments; flask R is clear so no mycoplasma test was ordered; flask S has a matching label so STR was unnecessary. Penicillin-streptomycin was added to P and Q until the clues diminished. The shared-medium lot, incubator, pipette and receipt records were not retained. All five were released for experiments.” Write a corrected evidence and handoff plan: identify visible clue limits; specify quarantine, dedicated mycoplasma and STR evidence; choose dispositions; reject masking; and list incoming-line and source-trace records.

rubric.criterion: Recognises the bacterial and fungal clue patterns without naming species from appearance, and connects them to testable medium, equipment and handling routes
Requires quarantine before identification and dedicated controlled mycoplasma evidence for clear flasks, with culture, PCR and DNA-stain limits stated correctly
Chooses discard/replacement for routine confirmed microbial contamination, identity hold for STR mismatch, documented review before release, and no successful antibiotic-masking pathway
Explains STR loci and allele calls, reference provenance and match/mismatch limits, including HeLa-era cross-contamination and the non-clearing role of the ICLAC register

Specifies an incident handoff with observations, tests/controls, dispositions, source hypotheses, linked records, cleaning requests and unresolved questions while excluding unnecessary donor or personal data

limitations: A zero-point self-check on a synthetic incident; it is not a grade or a competency record, and institutional procedures and responsible laboratory staff govern real contamination, disposal, rescue and authentication decisions.

cases.prompt: A colleague’s synthetic hPSC record says: “Line released from intake quarantine with STR match only; consent scope and MTA restrictions not reviewed. Destination matrix warmed, partially coated and dry. Day 1 density/morphology not recorded; day 2 feed missed without a deviation. Differentiated areas mostly removed but residual area not calculated. Routine passage made into a single-cell suspension with extensive trituration. Periodic mycoplasma and karyotype omitted because STR matched. Marker pattern reported as proof of functional pluripotency. Donor initials and an STR allele table pasted into the notes; medium/matrix lots and passage number absent.” Write a zero-point self-review that identifies the required gates and corrections, calculates what evidence would still be missing, and explains why the final claims are unjustified.

rubric.criterion: Requires consent/transfer/provenance review plus complete intake mycoplasma, STR, karyotype and undifferentiated-marker QC before quarantine release; excellent morphology cannot substitute

Corrects matrix handling and daily practice: cold liquid, complete even moist coating, daily density/morphology scoring, complete feeding, selective removal, residual/recurrent assessment and a deviation record
Restores small-clump rather than default single-cell passage with gentle handling, a prepared destination matrix and a feasible even allocation
Distinguishes mycoplasma, STR, karyotype and undifferentiated-marker evidence, repeats periodic QC and rejects marker-only functional-pluripotency or universal genomic-clearance claims
Removes donor-identifying and genomic-profile material from the exercise and requires synthetic aliases, actual medium/matrix lots, passage, observations, QC links and deviations

limitations: A zero-point self-check on an entirely synthetic record; it is not a grade, competency record, authorization or certification for hPSC work. Institutional governance, privacy rules, validated assays and supervised procedures govern real work.

cases.prompt: Zero-point synthetic self-check. A reviewer receives four observations: A1/P1 positive, A2/P1 positive, B1/P2 positive, B2/P2 negative, C1/P3 positive. Preparation records give P1/F1/matrix X1/reagent R1, P2/F2/X1/R1 and P3/F1/X2/R2. Formulation records give F1 = basal M17 + supplement S1, F2 = M17 + S2, and F3 = M18 + S3. Elsewhere, WCB W04 has been relabelled “new MCB” without a parent event; its previous PDL was 10.0 and the latest raw interval is N0 = 0.60 × 10⁶, Nf = 2.40 × 10⁶, but the ledger says +1/PDL 11.0. A vessel label reads only “LUMO, Alex”; another use record was silently overwritten from F9 to F1. Write a trace memo that (1) restores bank lineage and corrects the PDL, (2) performs the three-table join and counts positive vessels sharing the common basal-medium lot, (3) tests matrix, supplement and reagent alternatives, (4) explains why B2 matters, and (5) specifies label/ALCOA repairs and an outline-only incident/deviation handoff. State what remains unproven.

rubric.criterion: Restores the recorded MCB→WCB parent chain, rejects unsupported tier relabelling, recomputes log₂(2.40/0.60) = 2 and corrects cumulative PDL from 10.0 to 12.0 with an attributable audit trail
Joins A1/A2 through P1/F1, B1 through P2/F2 and C1 through P3/F1 to M17, counts four positive vessels and preserves distinct preparation, batch and received-lot identifiers
Rejects X1, R1 and S2 as universal positive exposures because C1 uses X2/R2/S1; retains B2 as an M17-exposed negative and identifies M17 as a lead rather than proven cause
Specifies durable unique label-to-ledger identifiers and ALCOA-based repairs that preserve original observations, timestamps, attribution, raw values, correction reasons and unresolved joins
Outlines containment, chronology, original evidence, linked scope including negatives, competing hypotheses and authorised local handoff without deep GLP/CLIA instruction or self-declared closure

limitations: A zero-point self-check using entirely synthetic records; it is not a grade, competency record, causal investigation or regulatory-quality-system exercise. Local procedures govern real records and contamination responses.
